question.text: The MAIN tax benefit of using a GIFT-IFSC feeder fund (as opposed to a Mauritius/Singapore feeder) is:

answer.text: GIFT-IFSC income qualifies for 100% tax holiday under Section 80LA of the Income-tax Act for any 10 consecutive years in a 15-year block, on specified income
GIFT-IFSC funds are fully exempt from SEBI regulations
GIFT-IFSC feeders face lower GST than Mauritius feeders
GIFT-IFSC allows leverage up to 10x unlike offshore

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 80LA of the Income-tax Act gives IFSC units a 100% tax holiday on specified income (including fund-management income) for any 10 consecutive years chosen within the first 15 years of operation — a very material benefit for a feeder fund. GIFT-IFSC is regulated by IFSCA (not SEBI) for fund management, under IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025. The Trap: Options B, C, D are fabricated. GIFT-IFSC is regulated (not exempt), GST treatment is jurisdictional, leverage rules follow IFSCA norms. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers Section 80LA; XIX-E tests it in the Cat III feeder context. Manager's Pro-Tip: Plan your 10-year tax-holiday window deliberately — it's a choice within the first 15 years. Aligning it with expected peak AUM gives the biggest rupee benefit.
